common.applies_to: Hybrid Tea, Floribunda or Grandiflora bush rose in New Zealand or Australia; answer to a common question
common.preserved_uncertainty: New Zealand: The times to stop come from two garden companies and one garden service, about a month apart (C-9). Other pages name no time to stop, and one says to deadhead throughout the flowering season. No New Zealand source gives a month to stop summer pruning (AF-25). Australia: No Australian source gives a month to stop deadheading (AF-29). Months for the summer trim differ by state, from January to April (C-11); the Western Australian society's aim is fresh growth, and the Victorian society trims only for a show or event. The areas the New South Wales society calls cool, mild and warm are not defined (AF-5). No Australian source gives a time to stop summer trimming.

items.text: Deadhead (remove the faded flowers) while the rose is flowering. Two garden companies say when to stop: one at the end of February, and one at the end of March, leaving the last flowers so that hips (the rose's fruit) can form. Months are only a guide.

In Auckland, one garden service says to stop deadheading from March, so that the rose can form hips and rest before winter. Another Auckland source says to keep removing dead flowers all through the flowering season. Months are only a guide.
I couldn't find when to stop summer pruning (a light prune in summer to encourage more flowers) in New Zealand. A local rose society is the place to ask.
I couldn't find a month to stop deadheading (cutting off the finished blooms) in Australia. A local rose society is the place to ask.
To bring on flowers in autumn, give the rose a light trim in summer or early autumn. This is done between January and March, depending on where you live. Months are only a guide.
In New South Wales, one rose society says to trim roses for flowers in autumn: in January in a cool area, early in February in a mild area, and in March in a warm area. Months are only a guide.
In Victoria, one rose society says to give a summer trim in February if you are timing the flowers for a show or special event. It also says to deadhead in April. Months are only a guide.

In South Australia, a light trim in late summer or early autumn brings on the autumn flowers. One nursery says mid February, and one rose society says one to two weeks after the February feed. Months are only a guide.
In Western Australia, one rose society says to give a light prune, taking off about one-third, in March or April, and to keep deadheading into May. Months are only a guide.
